label: Aquinas: immateriality explains knowing and its degree
paraphrase: Immateriality accounts for cognitive capacity and its degree: sense and intellect know in differing degrees of removal from matter; God, assumed supremely immaterial, is therefore said to have supreme knowledge.
note: Contextual reading of the Latin of ST I q.14 a.1 co. The general implication from two negative composition predicates to intellectual capacity, and the identification of those predicates with highest immateriality, are separate open analyst steps.
